title: Working Out the Employer Allowance a Till Transaction May Draw
content:
Employer allowance is spent against a till transaction already rung on an Employee Meal Account, and what it may meet is worked out from the ticket itself and from the allowance pot the account's ledger supports on the day.

## 1. The ticket and the ticket share

The ticket is the largest meal rung against payroll on the account, and the ticket share is that ticket taken at the share of an eligible ticket printed against the meal plan, rounded to two decimal places at that step. No window limits which till transaction the ticket may be: the largest meal rung against payroll on the account is taken however long ago it was rung.

## 2. The lots counted

The lots counted toward the allowance pot are the unspent allowance figure the account carries.

## 3. What is netted off, taken out and trimmed

Nothing is netted off the pot for allowance already applied. The employer's counter adds nothing to the pot. Nothing is taken out of the pot for guest meals. Nothing is taken out of the pot for meals rung outside the funded meal periods. Nothing is trimmed from the pot for a second counter at the site.

## 4. The allowance pot

The allowance pot is the lots counted plus what the employer's counter adds, less the amount netted off for allowance already applied, less the amount taken out for guest meals, less the amount taken out for meals outside the funded periods and less the amount trimmed for a second counter, and it is never read as less than nothing. What the employer's counter adds stands beside the employee's own lots in the pot rather than behind them, and is drawn on in the same call.

## 5. What is applied

The allowance applied to a till transaction is the ticket share, held to the per transaction ceiling printed against the plan and held again to the allowance pot worked out above, and it is never read as less than nothing. The figure is rounded to two decimal places at the end, over and above the rounding named above.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

Suppose the plan prints, for this illustration, a share of an eligible ticket of 80 percent and a per transaction ceiling of $10.00, the largest meal rung against payroll on the account came to $16.00, and the unspent allowance figure the account carries reads $34.00.

The ticket is $16.00 and the ticket share is $16.00 taken at 80 percent, or $12.80, rounded at that step. The lots counted are $34.00. Nothing is added by the counter, nothing is netted off, nothing is taken out for guest meals or for meals outside the funded periods, and nothing is trimmed, so the allowance pot is $34.00. The allowance applied is $12.80 held to the per transaction ceiling of $10.00, which gives $10.00, and held again to the pot of $34.00, which leaves it at $10.00. Rounded once more at the end, $10.00 is applied.

Had the pot come to $6.25 instead, the second holding would have taken the figure down to $6.25.


## How a window of calendar months is counted

A window of calendar months in this policy runs back from the day the account is worked and never from the turn of a named month: an entry falls inside such a window while fewer than that many whole months have gone by since the day it was booked, a whole month going by only when the same day of the month comes round again, so an entry exactly that many whole months old falls outside it, and an entry booked after the day the account is worked falls outside it too.
